title: Swallowing recovery after a stroke
what: A specialist checks how the person swallows and teaches exercises and techniques so food does not go into the airways. Safe food is chosen.
why: When after a stroke a person chokes, coughs while eating, or has trouble swallowing.
duration: a session usually takes 30 to 45 minutes; a course lasts weeks or months
tell_doctor: Whether the person chokes on food or water
Cough while eating, a wet voice after a swallow
Whether there was pneumonia after the stroke
How the person eats now: alone, or through a tube

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not give food or water until the specialist has checked swallowing. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Position
prepare.text: Eat sitting upright, not lying down.

prepare.title: Teeth
prepare.text: Dentures and mouth care are important. Bring the dentures.

steps: The specialist examines the mouth, tongue and voice
Gives a small amount of water or food of different thickness to try
Sometimes a swallowing test with a camera or X-ray is ordered
Teaches exercises for the tongue, lips and throat
Chooses the thickness of food and drinks
Shows the family how to feed safely
feel: The exercises do not hurt but are tiring
Thickened drinks taste unfamiliar at first
after: Eat sitting up, slowly, in small bites
Do not talk or watch TV while eating
Stay upright for 20 to 30 minutes after a meal
red_flags: Chokes, cannot cough it up and is gasping: call your local emergency number
Fever, cough, shortness of breath: pneumonia is possible, call your doctor
Refuses food and is losing weight quickly

faq.a: Thick liquid is easier to swallow and less likely to go into the airways.
In many people swallowing improves in the first weeks and months. Exercises help.

reminders.text: Swallowing session today. Bring dentures and discharge papers.
